deal_summary: A repeat-equipment request received an updated quote and moved to a procurement contact; that contact said several proposals were under review and promised an update, after which the view records only a seller follow-up (evidence 0, 1, 2, 3, 4).

customer_need.summary: A manager worklog says the customer wanted an item identical to a prior purchase and requested updated pricing; that repeat-purchase description is not independently detailed in customer-authored text (evidence 0).

deal_dynamics.early: The seller refreshed the quote and manager notes recorded that the offer was acceptable for consideration (evidence 0, 1).
deal_dynamics.middle: The customer routed the contract to procurement; the seller had only the project manager's email for follow-up (evidence 2).
deal_dynamics.late: The procurement contact said several offers were being considered and promised a response by the end of the week; a seller follow-up appears after that date with no reply in view (evidence 3, 4).

positive_signals: The manager log says the offer was acceptable for consideration and the customer requested contract preparation (evidence 1).
negative_signals: The procurement contact was evaluating several proposals, so the customer's decision was not settled (evidence 3).
customer_behavior.initiative: The customer routed the contract to procurement and gave the seller an expected response date (evidence 2, 3).
customer_behavior.decision_process: The decision had moved to a procurement group; the seller had no direct phone contact for the named project manager (evidence 2, 3).

strong_actions: The seller updated pricing, sent the contract to procurement, and acknowledged the customer's stated review date (evidence 0, 2, 3).
manager_behavior.follow_up_quality: The seller used the available email channel and followed up after the promised response date (evidence 3, 4).
manager_behavior.next_step_control: No revised decision date or procurement response is visible after the follow-up (evidence 4).

turning_points.description: The quote was updated for a repeat-equipment request (evidence 0).
The customer transferred the review to procurement and confirmed multiple offers were being considered (evidence 2, 3).
The seller followed up after the promised response date, with no reply in the available view (evidence 4).

primary_trajectory_explanation.explanation: The visible trajectory is a quote refresh followed by centralized procurement comparison. The customer's stated update date passed without a recorded decision in this view, so the purchase status remains unknown (evidence 0, 2, 3, 4).

secondary_factors: The claim that this was identical to an earlier purchase comes from manager worklog (evidence 0).
The record contains no direct technical objection or price objection from the procurement contact (evidence 3).

what_could_be_done: Ask procurement which comparison dimensions are still open and agree a new review date (evidence 3, 4).
Request a direct procurement contact route if email-only coordination continues (evidence 2).
limits: The customer's procurement group controlled the supplier comparison and response timing (evidence 2, 3).
No response after the last seller follow-up is shown (evidence 4).

uncertainties: The repeat-purchase description and early quote acceptance are manager-worklog claims (evidence 0, 1).
The view ends after a seller follow-up; the procurement decision and final deal status are unknown (evidence 3, 4).

evidence.paraphrase: Manager log says the request was for an item identical to one previously purchased and asks for current pricing.
Manager log says the offer was acceptable for consideration and records a planned follow-up with the purchasing contact.
Customer contact confirms the contract was sent to procurement and says only the procurement contact's email is available.
Procurement contact says several proposals are under review and promises an answer by the end of the week.
Seller asks how the procurement discussion went after the expected answer date.
